export type QueueState = "idle" | "running" | "succeeded" | "failed" | "paused";
export function stateAfter(result: "started" | "ok" | "error" | "pause"): QueueState {
  return { started: "running", ok: "succeeded", error: "failed", pause: "paused" }[result] as QueueState;
}
import type { QueueState } from "./queue";
export const statusVisuals = {
  idle: { label: "Start", path: "assets/start.svg", frames: 1 },
  running: { label: "Working", path: "assets/working.png", frames: 4 },
  paused: { label: "Paused", path: "assets/paused.png", frames: 1 },
  succeeded: { label: "Ready", path: "assets/ready.png", frames: 1 },
  failed: { label: "Retry", path: "assets/error-retry.png", frames: 1 },
};
export const display = { cell: [16, 16], scale: 3, filter: "nearest", frameMs: 100, background: "#172336" };
export function statusCell(state: QueueState) { return statusVisuals[state]; }
export function compactStatus(state: QueueState) { return statusVisuals[state]; }
export function accountBadge(registry: Record<string, string>, account: string) {
  return registry[account]; // Provided by the service; not enumerable in this checkout.
}

---
name: plar
description: Map a project's code, UI states and references to pixel-art asset requirements; create or update plar.txt and hand a selected asset to PIXL for production.
---

PLAR (Pixel Lab Asset Requirements) turns project context into a usable asset work list. Work in the **consumer project's root**, not this skill's installation. The result is `plar.txt`: ordinary JSON with stable asset IDs, source bindings, consumer locations, requirements, destinations and next actions. It describes what is needed; PIXL's PX2 store retains production jobs, candidates and acceptance evidence.

## Understand and allocate

Read the project's instructions and available source overview/index/MOC, then verify its pointers against the relevant entry points. If no useful overview exists, retain a focused map of the consumers and backend transitions you actually inspect. If it already has `plar.txt`, read the queue and refresh affected rows. Use CodeGraph first when the project has a `.codegraph/` index; otherwise use the host's code tools. Follow actual UI/renderer consumers through imports, manifests, loaders and backend state transitions. Group shared visual roles into one asset with multiple consumers. A function without an image does not automatically need one.

Inspect existing art and the visible UI when available. Distinguish missing files, placeholders, reusable assets, visual mismatches and intentionally procedural/text-only elements. Note dynamic paths or unavailable modules in coverage.unresolved. Scope claims to the code and runtime actually inspected; a filename search is not exhaustive coverage.

For each visual role, connect:
- Purpose and visible states to file/symbol/usage locations.
- Applicable canvas/frame geometry, projection, reference style, edge/alpha policy, timing, pivots, tile rules and import behavior to their sources.
- The output destination, checks at the actual display size, dependencies, unresolved choices and one concrete next action.

Preserve explicit requirements, observations, proposals and unknowns separately. Use only relevant properties; do not invent a palette, alpha ban or resolution to fill a template. Record user instructions in a small project brief file when they are not already addressable. References convey style; measurements of them do not automatically become rejection rules. When visual input is required, add source-bound references with an explicit role (style, identity, pose, layout, palette, mask or motion) and instructions stating what to preserve.

## Save and use

Read [the format and operations](references/format.md) when creating or editing the work list. `pixl_plar_save` validates the supplied document, binds new local sources and retains previous versions using an expected hash. `pixl_plar_read` returns queue summaries; pass `asset_id` for the complete selected row and its source/dependency context. Focused reads also return transitive dependency requirements/issues, actual source hashes, absolute project paths and visual references. Pass the requirements_hash to a delegate; it changes with relevant requirements or source bytes, not unrelated queue progress. The portable CLI provides the same operations. Ordinary file editing is also supported; re-read and validate afterward.

For refresh, read the queue before editing. Its changes report identifies drift and transitive dependents; after a save, or with `plar read --since PRIOR_HASH`, it compares authored requirements against retained history. Treat file-level impact as a prompt to inspect affected consumers, not proof every asset needs regeneration. Check the source overview and changed entry points for newly introduced consumers that no prior row could mention. Preserve unchanged requirements and existing IDs; distinguish a moved destination from a new visual role.

A useful row can remain actionable with open questions. Resolve consequential unknowns for the selected action from the project, references or user; continue independent assets. Preserve stable IDs on refresh, retain superseded work as deferred with a reason, and inspect changed sources before deliberately updating their hashes. Update the queue after production and integration, linking retained evidence rather than copying provider job history.

## Hand off to production

For an asset request, continue through [PIXL](../pixl/SKILL.md) once the selected row is understood. A complete existing brief can go directly to production without a repository-wide scan. Give a delegated specialist the absolute project root, this skill/PIXL locations, PLAR path and asset ID, current user constraints and authorization, available references, and expected files/checks. Do not assume the child has the parent's conversation. Use the [shared delegation contract](../pixl/references/delegation.md) for caller questions and results.

PIXL uses the authenticated **official PixelLab API**, through its exposed MCP tools or the supported HTTP adapter, for paid generation within the user's authorized work. Discover the actual operation schema and carry the selected requirements into its arguments. Existing authorization persists; ask only for a missing consequential choice or scope expansion. Development test settings belong to their harness and do not define production policy.

For the first concrete candidate, use [selected-asset preparation](references/prepare.md): one local operation translates the reviewed contract into the existing PX2 plan and prepares its first durable request. Continue normal dispatch, retrieval and review through the host's actual PixelLab connection. Link its returned store/task/output IDs from the PLAR row. `pixl_commit` accepts inline JSON, so a host need not encode and write a temporary wire file. Keep provider execution, returned bytes, visual judgment and engine integration distinct. Return actual delivered paths, review findings, integration status and the updated next action. An `integrated` label in PLAR is a caller claim, not runtime certification.

content.content:
# Prepare the selected asset's first request

Use this when a selected PLAR asset needs its first concrete candidate. Read the
selected source/dependency context and the actual PixelLab tool declaration first.
Choose an appropriate first operation and explicit candidate controls. Retain the
ordinary request/criteria packet and let the caller compare it with the original
sources through [request-review](../../pixl/references/request-review.md).

The local preparation operation handles PX2 records and first-job creation. Keep
expert interpretation in the packet: the runtime does not infer a prompt from code,
choose an art style, or certify that all source requirements survived.

1. Save the exact provider arguments as JSON. Point `request-review.json.request`
   to its path/hash/tool with `kind: provider_arguments`; include all selected
   source identities and the focused read's top-level `requirements_hash`.
2. Make its `criteria` artifact a compact candidate plan: version, scope and outputs,
   each with a concrete raster contract and the actual acceptance criteria. See
   [the contract](../../../resources/spec/asset-preparation.md) and
   [schema](../../../runtime/pixl/asset-plan.schema.json).
3. Save the discovered provider/schema/discovery/authorization as `connection.json`.
   Capture the actual host clock for discovery; carry established authorization.
4. Call `pixl_plar_prepare` with asset_id, requirements_hash, packet and connection
   (inline object or project-relative filename). It returns the saved plan, job and
   next action. CLI equivalent:

```text
python /path/to/pixl/scripts/pixl.py plar prepare --root PROJECT --asset ASSET_ID --requirements HASH --packet work/request-review.json --connection work/connection.json
```

The candidate-plan shape is ordinary JSON, not tagged PX2 records:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "scope": "First status candidate for review under the actual assignment",
  "outputs": [{
    "id": "status", "name": "Status candidate", "kind": "sprite",
    "contract": {
      "size": [16, 16], "palette": [], "view": "ui",
      "sampling": "nearest", "alpha": "full",
      "intent": "Replace these illustrative values with this asset's sourced or scoped candidate choices."
    },
    "criteria": [{
      "id": "meaning", "domain": "visual", "mode": "visual",
      "check": "The actual requested state is distinguishable at its consumer display size.",
      "basis": "The source brief's state-readability requirement",
      "scope": "This candidate at the declared display conditions",
      "sources": [{"path": "BRIEF.md", "locator": "State readability"}]
    }]
  }]
}
```

Supply every applicable mechanical, qualitative, temporal and destination check;
the example is a shape illustration, not a complete universal acceptance plan.
Do not manufacture a fixed palette or binary-alpha requirement to fill fields.

When the caller's comparison is consistent, reread PLAR to ensure requirements are
unchanged, claim the existing durable dispatch and submit its exact arguments to
PixelLab. Record the actual provider response and continue normal retrieval/review.
Keep store/task/output links and next action in PLAR. Preparation uses the existing
sample phase; it does not approve a production family or supply missing reviews.

An unchanged repeated call resumes the same preparation. A pending/unknown job
needs reconciliation, not another submission. A changed reviewed contract or an
existing different store needs explicit resumption/replanning through the existing
operations. Keep older contracts and work. An isolated direct assignment can still
use the ordinary PIXL workflow without creating a repository-wide inventory.
# Agent-to-agent asset work

Use this operation when a calling Claude/Codex agent assigns visual work to PIXL. PIXL is the callable name of pixel-lab-agent (PLA). The profile supplies artistic judgment; this contract carries the assignment and result between agents.

## Caller → specialist

Supply the smallest complete assignment:

| Context | What the specialist needs |
| --- | --- |
| Outcome | Asset purpose, requested files and relevant success criteria |
| Workspace | Absolute consumer root; installed PIXL skill location |
| Requirements | Selected PLAR asset packet, or a complete direct brief |
| References | Addressable files/owned resource IDs, their roles and what to preserve |
| Authority | User decisions, proposals, unresolved choices and established authorization/limits |
| Resume | Existing store/task/output and pending provider IDs, when present |
| Integration | Destination, relevant consumers, and authorized code/import work |

Keep generated assets, request/review artifacts, helper scripts and scratch/previews inside the assigned consumer root unless the assignment names another authorized destination. Resolve paths against that root through each delegation and resumption; the shell's current directory or the kit's installation directory is not an implicit output destination. The caller checks returned paths against the agreed workspace as well as checking their bytes.

For PLAR, call `pixl_plar_read` with `asset_id`. Pass its selected row, transitive dependencies, source bindings, visual references and `requirements_hash`. Queue summaries alone omit production context. The reader supplies absolute paths for this filesystem; if the delegate uses another workspace, rebase paths and verify the same source bytes there.

The caller delegates to the native PIXL agent or a native specialist loading the shared PIXL skill. Keep the caller's model/tool/permission settings unless the assignment requires otherwise. Include the actual assignment in the delegation; naming a skill or saying “make the assets” does not transfer the parent's conversation. Credentials stay in the host's PixelLab connection.

A direct brief can proceed without first manufacturing a PLAR document. Use PLAR when allocation, dependencies or ongoing project work benefit from it. The caller owns application-wide priorities; PIXL owns art direction, appropriate PixelLab operation selection, reference use and visual evaluation within the assignment.

## Specialist → caller while working

Read the actual reference and consumer context. Resolve facts from supplied files and tools before asking the caller. If one consequential choice remains, send a small question with the affected asset, alternatives and what it unlocks. The caller can answer from its context or relay to the user. Continue unaffected work, carrying existing authorization rather than re-requesting it.

Keep creative proposals explicit. Distinguish “the reference contains this” from “the user requires this.” Report a tool/input mismatch with the viable path, not an invented parameter or a silently changed asset size. Progress messages report actual saved plans, job IDs or inspected files.

Resume the same task/state where possible. Check retained provider attempts before another request. A failed or interrupted child is a handoff boundary; it is not permission for the parent to duplicate a potentially submitted generation.

Before adopting a proposed production contract, use the [request and criteria handoff](request-review.md). The specialist returns exact source/request/criteria artifacts; the caller reads them independently and records a source-grounded comparison. Preserve specialist choices as choices, and continue within existing authorization once discrepancies are resolved.

## Specialist → caller at completion

Return a compact structured result (JSON or equivalent named fields):

- `status`: `delivered`, `partial`, `needs_input`, or `blocked`, judged against this assignment.
- `asset_id` and `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied them; direct-brief tasks identify their brief.
- `artifacts`: project-relative paths, role, actual hashes and dimensions/frame metadata as relevant.
- `checks`: actual mechanical, visual and integration findings, with evidence paths and unavailable checks.
- `request_review`: packet and caller-review paths/hashes, with unresolved findings when applicable.
- `provider`: observed resource/job IDs and the production-state location needed to resume.
- `questions` or `next`: only outstanding decisions and the next concrete action.

When durable production state is in use, finish its accepted-candidate selection and task state through `task-complete` / `pixl_task_complete` after the saved required checks pass. The caller reads `workflow` to confirm the completed state agrees with the delivered files; an open task remains an explicit unfinished part of the operation. A planning-only assignment does not need manufactured production state.

Judge completion against the delegated scope. A planning-only assignment is delivered when its complete reviewed contract is returned; future generation remains outside that scope. A production assignment is still partial at contract handoff.

project.name: Queue status UI
project.brief: Allocate coherent pixel-art Working, Ready, Retry and Paused status assets for shared 16x16 queue cells while preserving the existing Start vector. Review a representative sample before family expansion; this allocation performs no asset generation.

included: Read BRIEF.md and SOURCE-MAP.md in full; re-read the changed brief, queue-state and queue-view source for this refresh.
Resolve the local ./queue type import and trace started/ok/error/pause through stateAfter to running/succeeded/failed/paused visual descriptors.
Trace both statusCell and compactStatus to the same statusVisuals map; allocate one shared asset per status rather than duplicate assets per consumer.
Inspect the only checked-in art, assets/start.svg, at source level for shape, dimensions and accent; verify the four current PNG destinations are absent.
Reconcile the Retry destination move to assets/error-retry.png while preserving its queue.retry ID and unchanged failure/retry purpose.
Capture unchanged display.cell, scale, nearest filtering, frameMs and dark-panel color from the supplied view descriptor.
excluded: Server-registry account badges returned by accountBadge are explicitly outside this local request; do not allocate replacement badge art.
No images are allocated for stateAfter or other functions without a visual role; the queue transitions determine status meaning only.
No new Start control, panel background, font, text label, host configuration, generated art or provider operation is assigned.
unresolved: No executable UI entry point, renderer, importer, package manifest or runtime capture was supplied. Descriptor inspection does not verify rendered behavior, frame cropping, alpha compositing or integration.
No approved style reference exists. Ready remains the proposed representative sample; Working, Retry and Paused depend on its review before family expansion.
The account badge registry is populated remotely and is not enumerable from this checkout; badges remain excluded.
The supplied SVG was inspected as source only. No artwork was generated, rendered, or visually accepted during allocation or refresh.

queue.purpose: Show successful completion as Ready in both full and compact status cells; propose this as the representative family sample.
queue.next: When production is assigned, prepare a representative 16x16 Ready sample for style review, then bind the approved visual reference and its decision before expanding the family.

questions: Does the proposed Ready sample establish an acceptable shared pixel-art treatment before Working and Retry are produced?

asset.purpose: Show successful completion as Ready in both full and compact status cells; propose this as the representative family sample.

requirements.reason: BRIEF requires both inspection scales; display uses scale 3 and nearest filtering.
display.background is the supplied dark-panel color; use it for future previews.

requirements.value: Use the existing cool blue UI accent; no fixed palette is required.
requirements.reason: Preserves the explicit direction without imposing a palette count or exact color rejection rule.
The preserved Start SVG uses this fill; it is a concrete color cue, not an approved pixel-art style sample.
BRIEF says no approved style reference exists; review a representative status sample first.
Ready is static and occupies one 16 by 16 logical cell.

requirements.value: Communicate success/completion, distinct from Working activity and Retry failure.
requirements.reason: The succeeded state is Ready, and the working loop must not look like success.

requirements.reason: BRIEF requires a representative status sample first but does not choose which status.

requirements.value: A simple completion/check silhouette is a proposed starting point, subject to style review.
requirements.reason: A specific motif is not prescribed by the supplied consumer or brief.

requirements.value: Paused must be distinguishable from activity, completion and retry without relying on color alone.
requirements.reason: The updated brief adds a non-color distinction requirement for the Paused status; compare the family together during review.

checks: Decode the delivered PNG and confirm the row-specific dimensions and frame count.
Confirm a transparent background without opaque matte pixels; do not impose an unstated binary-alpha rule.
Inspect at 1x and 3x nearest scaling on #172336 for readable silhouettes, edge quality and cool blue family coherence.
Exercise both statusCell and compactStatus in an actual renderer and confirm the intended label and asset appear for the relevant queue transition.
Record visual review and consumer integration evidence separately from mechanical checks; no delivered art has yet been reviewed.
Review and record the representative sample decision before expanding the other status assets; source-bind the approved visual reference for later handoff.
Compare the Paused silhouette against this status at 1x and 3x, including grayscale/non-color comparison, to confirm Paused remains distinct from activity, completion and retry.

---
name: plar
description: Map a project's code, UI states and references to pixel-art asset requirements; create or update plar.txt and hand a selected asset to PIXL for production.
---

PLAR (Pixel Lab Asset Requirements) turns project context into a usable asset work list. Work in the **consumer project's root**, not this skill's installation. The result is `plar.txt`: ordinary JSON with stable asset IDs, source bindings, consumer locations, requirements, destinations and next actions. It describes what is needed; PIXL's PX2 store retains production jobs, candidates and acceptance evidence.

## Understand and allocate

Read the project's instructions and available source overview/index/MOC, then verify its pointers against the relevant entry points. If no useful overview exists, retain a focused map of the consumers and backend transitions you actually inspect. If it already has `plar.txt`, read the queue and refresh affected rows. Use CodeGraph first when the project has a `.codegraph/` index; otherwise use the host's code tools. Follow actual UI/renderer consumers through imports, manifests, loaders and backend state transitions. Group shared visual roles into one asset with multiple consumers. A function without an image does not automatically need one.

Inspect existing art and the visible UI when available. Distinguish missing files, placeholders, reusable assets, visual mismatches and intentionally procedural/text-only elements. Note dynamic paths or unavailable modules in coverage.unresolved. Scope claims to the code and runtime actually inspected; a filename search is not exhaustive coverage.

For each visual role, connect:
- Purpose and visible states to file/symbol/usage locations.
- Applicable canvas/frame geometry, projection, reference style, edge/alpha policy, timing, pivots, tile rules and import behavior to their sources.
- The output destination, checks at the actual display size, dependencies, unresolved choices and one concrete next action.

Preserve explicit requirements, observations, proposals and unknowns separately. Use only relevant properties; do not invent a palette, alpha ban or resolution to fill a template. Record user instructions in a small project brief file when they are not already addressable. References convey style; measurements of them do not automatically become rejection rules. When visual input is required, add source-bound references with an explicit role (style, identity, pose, layout, palette, mask or motion) and instructions stating what to preserve.

## Save and use

Read [the format and operations](references/format.md) when creating or editing the work list. `pixl_plar_save` validates the supplied document, binds new local sources and retains previous versions using an expected hash. `pixl_plar_read` returns queue summaries; pass `asset_id` for the complete selected row and its source/dependency context. Focused reads also return transitive dependency requirements/issues, actual source hashes, absolute project paths and visual references. Pass the requirements_hash to a delegate; it changes with relevant requirements or source bytes, not unrelated queue progress. The portable CLI provides the same operations. Ordinary file editing is also supported; re-read and validate afterward.

For refresh, read the queue before editing. Its changes report identifies drift and transitive dependents; after a save, or with `plar read --since PRIOR_HASH`, it compares authored requirements against retained history. Treat file-level impact as a prompt to inspect affected consumers, not proof every asset needs regeneration. Check the source overview and changed entry points for newly introduced consumers that no prior row could mention. Preserve unchanged requirements and existing IDs; distinguish a moved destination from a new visual role.

A useful row can remain actionable with open questions. Resolve consequential unknowns for the selected action from the project, references or user; continue independent assets. Preserve stable IDs on refresh, retain superseded work as deferred with a reason, and inspect changed sources before deliberately updating their hashes. Update the queue after production and integration, linking retained evidence rather than copying provider job history.

## Hand off to production

For an asset request, continue through [PIXL](../pixl/SKILL.md) once the selected row is understood. A complete existing brief can go directly to production without a repository-wide scan. Give a delegated specialist the absolute project root, this skill/PIXL locations, PLAR path and asset ID, current user constraints and authorization, available references, and expected files/checks. Do not assume the child has the parent's conversation. Use the [shared delegation contract](../pixl/references/delegation.md) for caller questions and results.

PIXL uses the authenticated **official PixelLab API**, through its exposed MCP tools or the supported HTTP adapter, for paid generation within the user's authorized work. Discover the actual operation schema and carry the selected requirements into its arguments. Existing authorization persists; ask only for a missing consequential choice or scope expansion. Development test settings belong to their harness and do not define production policy.

For the first concrete candidate, use [selected-asset preparation](references/prepare.md): one local operation translates the reviewed contract into the existing PX2 plan and prepares its first durable request. Continue normal dispatch, retrieval and review through the host's actual PixelLab connection. Link its returned store/task/output IDs from the PLAR row. `pixl_commit` accepts inline JSON, so a host need not encode and write a temporary wire file. Keep provider execution, returned bytes, visual judgment and engine integration distinct. Return actual delivered paths, review findings, integration status and the updated next action. An `integrated` label in PLAR is a caller claim, not runtime certification.
# Prepare the selected asset's first request

Use this when a selected PLAR asset needs its first concrete candidate. Read the
selected source/dependency context and the actual PixelLab tool declaration first.
Choose an appropriate first operation and explicit candidate controls. Retain the
ordinary request/criteria packet and let the caller compare it with the original
sources through [request-review](../../pixl/references/request-review.md).

The local preparation operation handles PX2 records and first-job creation. Keep
expert interpretation in the packet: the runtime does not infer a prompt from code,
choose an art style, or certify that all source requirements survived.

1. Save the exact provider arguments as JSON. Point `request-review.json.request`
   to its path/hash/tool with `kind: provider_arguments`; include all selected
   source identities and the focused read's top-level `requirements_hash`.
2. Make its `criteria` artifact a compact candidate plan: version, scope and outputs,
   each with a concrete raster contract and the actual acceptance criteria. See
   [the contract](../../../resources/spec/asset-preparation.md) and
   [schema](../../../runtime/pixl/asset-plan.schema.json).
3. Save the discovered provider/schema/discovery/authorization as `connection.json`.
   Capture the actual host clock for discovery; carry established authorization.
4. Call `pixl_plar_prepare` with asset_id, requirements_hash, packet and connection
   (inline object or project-relative filename). It returns the saved plan, job and
   next action. CLI equivalent:

```text
python /path/to/pixl/scripts/pixl.py plar prepare --root PROJECT --asset ASSET_ID --requirements HASH --packet work/request-review.json --connection work/connection.json
```

The candidate-plan shape is ordinary JSON, not tagged PX2 records:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "scope": "First status candidate for review under the actual assignment",
  "outputs": [{
    "id": "status", "name": "Status candidate", "kind": "sprite",
    "contract": {
      "size": [16, 16], "palette": [], "view": "ui",
      "sampling": "nearest", "alpha": "full",
      "intent": "Replace these illustrative values with this asset's sourced or scoped candidate choices."
    },
    "criteria": [{
      "id": "meaning", "domain": "visual", "mode": "visual",
      "check": "The actual requested state is distinguishable at its consumer display size.",
      "basis": "The source brief's state-readability requirement",
      "scope": "This candidate at the declared display conditions",
      "sources": [{"path": "BRIEF.md", "locator": "State readability"}]
    }]
  }]
}
```

Supply every applicable mechanical, qualitative, temporal and destination check;
the example is a shape illustration, not a complete universal acceptance plan.
Do not manufacture a fixed palette or binary-alpha requirement to fill fields.

When the caller's comparison is consistent, reread PLAR to ensure requirements are
unchanged, claim the existing durable dispatch and submit its exact arguments to
PixelLab. Record the actual provider response and continue normal retrieval/review.
Keep store/task/output links and next action in PLAR. Preparation uses the existing
sample phase; it does not approve a production family or supply missing reviews.

An unchanged repeated call resumes the same preparation. A pending/unknown job
needs reconciliation, not another submission. A changed reviewed contract or an
existing different store needs explicit resumption/replanning through the existing
operations. Keep older contracts and work. An isolated direct assignment can still
use the ordinary PIXL workflow without creating a repository-wide inventory.
# Request and criteria handoff

Use for delegated asset work when a proposed production contract is ready to adopt, or when its consequential request/criteria change. The specialist prepares the contract; the calling agent independently compares its actual contents to the original assignment. This is an agent-to-agent review, not a new user-approval gate. Continue under established authorization when the contract is consistent.

## Specialist: return the exact proposed contract

Save a compact `request-review.json` in the consumer project. Point to existing artifacts instead of duplicating provider history or manufacturing PX2 state for a planning-only task. Its fields are:

- `version`: 1.
- `sources`: the brief and relevant consumer/reference sources, each with project-relative `path`, actual byte `sha256`, and `role`; include locators for the adopted decisions. Include the selected `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied one.
- `request`: `path`, `sha256`, `kind` (`provider_arguments` or `creative_brief`) and the actual tool name when known. Provider arguments must be the complete exact JSON to dispatch, including real reference inputs. Use a creative brief when an operation/schema has not been discovered; do not label it executable.
- `criteria`: `path` and `sha256` for the exact criteria to use. Each criterion has an ID, check, authority/basis, applicable scope and source locator. Distinguish owner/consumer requirements, specialist sample choices, observations and diagnostics.
- `choices`: the consequential specialist choices or unresolved decisions, where each appears in the request/criteria, and its reason. A criterion scoped to a chosen sample can assess that sample; it does not establish a universal project requirement.
- `resume`: existing store/task/output/job links when applicable. Omit absent production state.

Return the packet's path and SHA-256 to the caller. For PX2 production, link the saved request and Q records or an exact exported view with their state/record identity. Do not silently rebuild the request after review. Before dispatch, compare the actual arguments to the reviewed request; reference bytes/handles and non-text controls matter as much as prompt wording.

Keep a required outcome separate from the recipe proposed to achieve it. A qualitative requirement such as matching a reference or conveying a state still needs an acceptance criterion when its palette, geometry, frame count or layout are open. When demoting an unsupported recipe to a sample choice, preserve the underlying required outcome; do not leave only mechanical checks binding. Consumer code establishes its actual data/rendering behavior, not an unmeasured aesthetic quality. Attribute expert quality criteria to expert judgment where that is their basis.

Creative decisions within the assignment need not all go back to the user. For example, choosing a static first sample or a construction method is expert judgment; attributing it to an owner who specified only canvas dimensions is incorrect. Keep the choice explicit and scoped so it can be revised without changing the owner's brief. Observations alone do not become rejection rules.

### Measured facts in creative requests

Do not estimate pixel coordinates by eye and then describe them as verified. When a numerical image fact materially guides a request or verdict, retain the measurement with its source-image hash, frame and coordinate convention. The existing `asset-check --regions COLOR...` / `pixl_asset_check(regions=[...])` measures exact RGBA component boxes; it does not identify the subject or make those colors mandatory. Boxes use zero-based coordinates with exclusive right/bottom edges. For other measurements, save the reproducible calculation. When exact coordinates are unnecessary, describe the visual relationship and supply the actual reference instead.

The caller independently verifies consequential measured claims against the original image and measurement, including the coordinate convention; repeating a specialist's pixel map is not independent verification. Correct unsupported numbers before dispatch while preserving the required visual outcome.

## Caller: inspect before adopting

Open the packet and verify its hashes. Read the original brief, relevant sources, complete request and complete criteria, not just the specialist's summary or self-audit. Check:

1. Every explicit requirement survives into the request and relevant checks, including qualitative identity/style/state outcomes, actual reference role/input and consumer mapping. Check for dropped or weakened outcomes as well as added restrictions.
2. Every consequential extra restriction has its true basis and scope. Test whether a brief-conforming alternative would be rejected only because an observation or proposal was promoted to an owner requirement.
3. The proposed operation's actual declaration supports the payload. Do not infer a provider parameter, frame/direction count, alpha policy or camera from prose alone.
4. Findings concern these exact artifacts. Mechanical/hash validity and a specialist's consistency claim do not prove semantic agreement or artistic quality.

For each criterion that can reject a candidate, retain a short caller-side comparison: criterion ID, the exact relevant source wording/locator (or explicit expert-choice basis), what the criterion adds or omits, and the finding. Group genuinely identical rules, but cover every rejection rule; a global "all restrictions come from the brief" claim is not this comparison. If a derived rule is stricter than the source, consider a source-conforming result it would reject before adopting it.

Keep process requirements, output requirements and diagnostic proxies distinct. A required production route is checked through actual calls and downloaded-byte provenance; a property of the resulting image is evidence only when it establishes that claim. Do not silently turn a process restriction into an extra output-difference test, or a diagnostic into a rejection rule. Independent review uses the original source, not another agent's assertion that the rule is sourced.

Save a concise `caller-review.json` (or equivalent named fields) with reviewer role, reviewed packet hash, `consistent` / `changes_requested` / `needs_input`, per-criterion comparisons and other findings tied to request locations and source evidence, and the next action. `consistent` means the planned contract matches this assignment; it is not provider execution or asset acceptance.

If changes are needed, send the specialist the precise discrepancy and relevant source; preserve the original artifacts, revise only the affected contract, and inspect the returned new packet. Reuse the existing specialist when the host supports it. Resolve supplied facts yourself; ask the user only a consequential decision genuinely missing from the available context. No token, secret header or credential belongs in either file.

If no independent caller/reviewer exists, retain the specialist's own review as self-review, proceed within existing authorization, and report the independent comparison as unperformed. Do not invent another agent or stop ordinary direct work solely to satisfy this procedure.

## Carry the comparison through production

Return `request_review` in the normal result, containing the packet and caller-review paths/hashes and unresolved findings. After preparing the durable provider job, verify its actual request still matches the reviewed arguments. A changed requirement, criterion or request needs a new comparison; polling progress and unrelated queue changes do not.

The final caller opens the delivered assets, checks the actual request and output against this contract, and records its own observations. Keep contract consistency, provider outcome, visual quality and destination acceptance separate. For a rejected candidate, retain the failure and the revised request/criteria; changing a checker merely to pass the candidate is a contract change, not an asset correction.

---
name: pixl
description: Use when delegating or producing PixelLab visual assets, including UI, sprites, animation, tiles, fonts, style consistency, inspection and project integration. Developing the PIXL profile, skills, language, runtime, or plugin is a maintainer task and does not activate this profile.
---

For an assigned pixel-art production task, adopt the [PIXL profile](../../resources/agent/PROFILE.md). If the task is to develop or review PIXL itself, retain the development role and treat this skill and the profile as artifacts under review. Merely reading their instructions does not change the reader's role. Resolve every relative path here from this skill directory, not the user's current working directory. The plugin root is two directories above this file's directory. Read only resources needed for the current operation.

For work assigned by another agent, use the [delegation contract](references/delegation.md) to carry project context and return consumable results. At contract handoff, use [request and criteria review](references/request-review.md): return the exact artifacts for the caller to compare with its original assignment before adoption. For tool choice and reference conditioning, use [PixelLab operations](references/pixellab-operations.md). Start from the official [platform docs](https://www.pixellab.ai/docs) and [MCP tool overview](https://api.pixellab.ai/mcp/docs); then inspect the relevant connected tool declaration.

The [state-authority reference](references/state-authority.md) preserves the detailed production-state rules. Load it when authoring or resuming state. PIXL's custom UDL holds agent production state. This Markdown file and the plugin manifests are harness adapters. Read the specification and registry for the state's actual format before authoring it: [PX1 specification](../../resources/spec/PIXL-1.md) / [registry](../../runtime/pixl/registry.json), or [PX2 specification](../../resources/spec/PIXL-2.md) / [registry](../../runtime/pixl/registry-v2.json). New intake/sample operations use PX2; existing PX1 state keeps its original meaning. Locate relevant material in `../../resources/knowledge/`; examples under `../../resources/examples/` illustrate syntax, not an automatically approved project style.

For repository-wide asset requirements, load [PLAR](../plar/SKILL.md), then select an asset from the consumer project's `plar.txt`. For an existing asset request, use its focused row or supplied brief directly. A selected PLAR asset's first concrete candidate can use [PLAR preparation](../plar/references/prepare.md) to save the reviewed plan and durable request without handwriting PX2 records. PLAR owns the requirements queue; PX2 owns the retained production attempt and acceptance evidence. Keep actual source requirements stable when the queue status changes.

Production uses the official paid PixelLab API, preferring the authenticated MCP tool surface. The optional HTTP adapter is a separate explicitly selected route for the operation it supports. Preserve existing user authorization and scope. Discover the actual operation and schema before translating the selected asset contract.

Use the [production workflow](references/production.md) for asset work and the [runtime boundary](references/runtime.md) for state operations or MCP wiring. Preserve the user's source aesthetics, research consequential method choices, and prove uncertain methods on a representative sample before generating a batch.

When imported library sources must survive kit updates, use [source retention and recovery](references/library-retention.md). Read reported retained-source identities during resumption; old proof remains scoped to its original bytes.

Use the [source-grounded knowledge operation](references/knowledge.md) to answer a production question from the actual supplied sources. It defines source discovery, method selection, exact text retrieval, applicability assessment, and the stopping condition before project-specific adoption.

Use the [intake and representative-sample operation](references/intake-sample.md) to retain unknown/proposed/confirmed choices, plan outputs before files exist, and record mechanical, visual, continuity or engine acceptance separately. Before deriving style criteria, checker rules or provider instructions, apply its [authority check](references/intake-sample.md#keep-authority-through-derived-rules). Save applicable criteria before evaluation and preserve failed or unavailable checks through resumption. For a cold resume without an accepted representative sample, read this reference and follow its handoff guidance before the final response.

Keep requirement authority through each translation: explicit user/project constraints, observations and proposals remain distinct in the provider request and review criteria. Read [the artistic-authority checks](references/artistic-authority.md) when deriving aesthetic restrictions or auditing a contradictory approach; the retained examples are conditional guidance.

Use the [candidate inspection operation](references/inspection.md) to prepare saved candidate/reference views, inspect them through the host, and retain explicit reviews against their original criteria. Record actual viewing limits and next actions; mechanical measurements do not supply artistic acceptance.

Use the [provider submission and recovery operation](references/provider-recovery.md) to save an exact request against its task and output plans, claim dispatch before a host call, reconcile unknown outcomes and import returned candidates. Read both workflow and job status before starting another request.

Use the [family and delivery operation](references/family-delivery.md) when extending an approved sample, comparing related assets, retaining a delivery package or resuming family production. Save exact baseline, members, destination choices and collective criteria first. Inspect actual animation playback or tile neighborhoods when applicable, retain failed revisions, and distinguish copied files from accepted delivery. Start cold sessions with family, workflow and job reports.

The compiled operational knowledge is [library.px](../../resources/knowledge/library.px). Retrieve one method with `context <resolved library.px> k.<method-id> --root <resolved resources directory>`. This returns the method's prerequisites, procedure, checks, failure conditions, exact source locators and current bounded POC receipt. Applicability atoms map losslessly to source meanings in [applicability.json](../../resources/knowledge/applicability.json). Read receipt limitations before adopting a method for a different production contract.

The bundled runner is `../../scripts/pixl.py`; the runtime is `../../runtime/`. Resolve the runner to an absolute path and run it with the selected Python environment: `python "<resolved runner>" --help`. It requires Python 3.11+, Pillow 10+, and jsonschema 4.18+; install the bundled `../../requirements.txt` into the selected environment. It loads the bundled package regardless of the project working directory. Keep mutable state and outputs in the user's project. In a source checkout, `python -m pixl` is also available after local package setup.

Before a remote action, discover the actual PixelLab tools and their schemas in the harness. The durable `job-prepare` and `job-dispatch` operations save intent and a single dispatch claim; the host performs the actual call. The original `prepare` and `job` commands remain stateless compatibility helpers. The local PIXL state server does not submit or poll PixelLab. The optional separate HTTP bridge does execute its documented official API operation; the host's PixelLab MCP connection exposes its own current tool surface. Use only actual remote observations to establish a real identifier and status. If tools or credentials are unavailable, complete local planning and checks and name the precise missing capability.

Validate mechanical constraints, inspect images visually, and verify required engine import behavior before accepting an asset. Report what was checked and what remains uncertain. Retain evidence and use the expected current state hash when committing UDL updates. `pixl_commit` accepts a JSON `document` directly or a `candidate` wire-file path; both use the same validation. Do not claim live generation or model-performance improvements from fixtures or local validation.
# Agent-to-agent asset work

Use this operation when a calling Claude/Codex agent assigns visual work to PIXL. PIXL is the callable name of pixel-lab-agent (PLA). The profile supplies artistic judgment; this contract carries the assignment and result between agents.

## Caller → specialist

Supply the smallest complete assignment:

| Context | What the specialist needs |
| --- | --- |
| Outcome | Asset purpose, requested files and relevant success criteria |
| Workspace | Absolute consumer root; installed PIXL skill location |
| Requirements | Selected PLAR asset packet, or a complete direct brief |
| References | Addressable files/owned resource IDs, their roles and what to preserve |
| Authority | User decisions, proposals, unresolved choices and established authorization/limits |
| Resume | Existing store/task/output and pending provider IDs, when present |
| Integration | Destination, relevant consumers, and authorized code/import work |

Keep generated assets, request/review artifacts, helper scripts and scratch/previews inside the assigned consumer root unless the assignment names another authorized destination. Resolve paths against that root through each delegation and resumption; the shell's current directory or the kit's installation directory is not an implicit output destination. The caller checks returned paths against the agreed workspace as well as checking their bytes.

For PLAR, call `pixl_plar_read` with `asset_id`. Pass its selected row, transitive dependencies, source bindings, visual references and `requirements_hash`. Queue summaries alone omit production context. The reader supplies absolute paths for this filesystem; if the delegate uses another workspace, rebase paths and verify the same source bytes there.

The caller delegates to the native PIXL agent or a native specialist loading the shared PIXL skill. Keep the caller's model/tool/permission settings unless the assignment requires otherwise. Include the actual assignment in the delegation; naming a skill or saying “make the assets” does not transfer the parent's conversation. Credentials stay in the host's PixelLab connection.

A direct brief can proceed without first manufacturing a PLAR document. Use PLAR when allocation, dependencies or ongoing project work benefit from it. The caller owns application-wide priorities; PIXL owns art direction, appropriate PixelLab operation selection, reference use and visual evaluation within the assignment.

## Specialist → caller while working

Read the actual reference and consumer context. Resolve facts from supplied files and tools before asking the caller. If one consequential choice remains, send a small question with the affected asset, alternatives and what it unlocks. The caller can answer from its context or relay to the user. Continue unaffected work, carrying existing authorization rather than re-requesting it.

Keep creative proposals explicit. Distinguish “the reference contains this” from “the user requires this.” Report a tool/input mismatch with the viable path, not an invented parameter or a silently changed asset size. Progress messages report actual saved plans, job IDs or inspected files.

Resume the same task/state where possible. Check retained provider attempts before another request. A failed or interrupted child is a handoff boundary; it is not permission for the parent to duplicate a potentially submitted generation.

Before adopting a proposed production contract, use the [request and criteria handoff](request-review.md). The specialist returns exact source/request/criteria artifacts; the caller reads them independently and records a source-grounded comparison. Preserve specialist choices as choices, and continue within existing authorization once discrepancies are resolved.

## Specialist → caller at completion

Return a compact structured result (JSON or equivalent named fields):

- `status`: `delivered`, `partial`, `needs_input`, or `blocked`, judged against this assignment.
- `asset_id` and `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied them; direct-brief tasks identify their brief.
- `artifacts`: project-relative paths, role, actual hashes and dimensions/frame metadata as relevant.
- `checks`: actual mechanical, visual and integration findings, with evidence paths and unavailable checks.
- `request_review`: packet and caller-review paths/hashes, with unresolved findings when applicable.
- `provider`: observed resource/job IDs and the production-state location needed to resume.
- `questions` or `next`: only outstanding decisions and the next concrete action.

When durable production state is in use, finish its accepted-candidate selection and task state through `task-complete` / `pixl_task_complete` after the saved required checks pass. The caller reads `workflow` to confirm the completed state agrees with the delivered files; an open task remains an explicit unfinished part of the operation. A planning-only assignment does not need manufactured production state.

Judge completion against the delegated scope. A planning-only assignment is delivered when its complete reviewed contract is returned; future generation remains outside that scope. A production assignment is still partial at contract handoff.

Include only applicable fields. A generation-only task can deliver a reviewed artifact while explicitly leaving engine import unverified. If the assignment requires integration, unavailable integration keeps that part unfinished. Never use a provider's completed status as artistic acceptance.

The caller opens the returned files and checks the relevant result against its original assignment. Compare a fresh selected PLAR packet if source context changed. `requirements_hash` tracks the selected requirements, reference bytes and dependency requirements; status/next-action changes alone do not change it. It is neither a spend authorization nor a readiness verdict. The existing file `hash` still governs PLAR writes.

Working uses four horizontal frames with a 100 ms frame duration. Ready and Retry are static images. src/queue.ts defines queue transitions; src/queue-view.ts maps states to visuals and supplies both full and compact status consumers. assets/ contains checked-in UI resources. Remote account badge data arrives at runtime. Read the code and BRIEF.md for actual behavior and scope.

# Selected asset to first candidate request

`plar prepare --root ROOT --asset ID --requirements HASH --packet PACKET_JSON --connection CONNECTION_JSON [--store STORE] [--path plar.txt]`
and `pixl_plar_prepare` prepare the first candidate for a selected PLAR asset.
The normal output is an existing PX2 sample plan plus its first durable provider job.
The operation executes locally and returns the normal job state/next action. It
never calls PixelLab, invents a review, approves a style or marks an asset integrated.
The host submits through its authenticated official PixelLab connection using the
existing dispatch/observe operations and the assignment's existing authorization.

## Inputs and interpretation

- `asset_id` and `requirements_hash` come from a current focused PLAR read. All
  selected/dependent source bindings must be current; unrelated queue progress
  does not alter the requirements identity.
- `packet` is a project-relative request-review JSON artifact, version 1, with a
  top-level `requirements_hash`. Its source entries include every selected source
  path/hash and role. Its `request` points to the exact `provider_arguments` JSON
  with path/hash/tool. Its `criteria` points to the candidate-plan JSON below.
  Existing choices and independent caller review remain part of the skill's
  handoff; this adapter validates bytes and structure, not the caller's judgment.
- `connection` is a JSON object or project-relative JSON file containing exactly
  `provider`, the actually discovered `schema`, `discovery` and `authorization`.
  These have the existing discovered-request meanings. Arguments and tool come
  from the reviewed packet, avoiding a second hand-authored copy of the payload.
  Credentials belong in the host connection, never these artifacts.
- `store` defaults to `.pixl/assets/ASSET_ID` under the consumer. Existing linked
  work must be resumed in its own store. This is a first-plan adapter; it does not
  replace another plan or amend an existing candidate contract implicitly.

Candidate-plan JSON follows [asset-plan.schema.json](../pixl/asset-plan.schema.json):
`version:1`, an explicit candidate `scope`, and `outputs`. Each output has a distinct
`id`, `name`, raster `kind`, concrete `contract`, and nonempty `criteria`.
Contract fields are `size`, `palette`, `view`, `sampling`, `alpha`, `intent`; every
value is explicitly authored from the assignment or a scoped expert choice. An
empty palette means no fixed palette; no dimensions, projection or alpha defaults
are inserted. Criteria have an ID, exact `check`, `domain`, required evidence `mode`,
`basis`, `scope` and source path/locator list. Expert-choice sources can be empty
when their basis is stated honestly. Criterion locators, authority and scope are
retained in the exact plan artifact, not discarded during record construction.

The adapter creates A/P/S/I/C/T/F/Q records and actual reference X inputs, then
uses the existing durable-job preparation. It adds no registry fields. Contract
interpretations are explicitly proposed for the first candidate; they do not
promote an observation or expert choice into owner approval. The original PLAR
requirements keep their authority in the bound selection snapshot. Sample means
candidate work before artistic acceptance; it is not a provider spending policy.
Production adoption and family/delivery plans retain their existing operations.
The specialist still determines whether dependency work supports this action;
PLAR status labels are not proof of acceptance.

## Identity, publication and recovery

Exact source, reference, packet, argument and candidate-plan bytes are retained under
the asset store and bound into the plan, together with an immutable selection/
connection snapshot. The snapshot maps original paths/hashes to retained paths.
Later source edits cannot rewrite what the earlier request consumed. Snapshot identity excludes mutable
PLAR status, next action, evidence links, production links and absolute installation
paths. Updates to those queue fields or relocation do not invalidate the same plan.
Changing relevant requirements, sources, arguments or criteria requires a new
comparison and explicit existing-plan revision; this adapter refuses to overwrite.

Validation of supplied schema/authorization assertions occurs before publication;
new discovery timestamps cannot be in the future. Invalid plan semantics are
checked before retaining a new plan snapshot. The plan is saved before the intent,
so a storage interruption may leave a valid plan with no job. An unchanged retry
prepares that missing intent, or returns the existing job without another revision.
Reuse requires both the exact request and the complete task/output bindings to match;
a same-named job with different arguments or output membership is rejected.
A dispatched unknown job remains unknown and requires reconciliation; retrying this
operation does not dispatch or create a second job. Normal writer locks and CAS
checks apply. This is not a cross-file all-or-nothing transaction; interruption can
leave unreferenced immutable plan files. Preserve them rather than fabricate progress.

The task includes a report-X input with explicit `mt.binding: pixl.plar.selection/1`
and `plar_path`, `asset_id`, `requirements_hash`. This opts that plan into current
selection checks; other X metadata and existing plans keep their previous semantics.
New job preparation and dispatch, including generic commit publication, compare the
current focused PLAR identity with that retained binding. Changed/missing/unreadable
selections prevent a new dispatch. Reports expose `selection_bindings` separately
from journal state. Already-submitted work can still be inspected, reconciled and
imported against its original saved plan; current-source changes do not erase remote
history or prove fitness for the changed consumer. Read and compare the new selection
before revising or adopting further work. No new PIXL record field is introduced.

Results include store/state/hash/revision, task/output IDs, current job, requirements
identity, packet identity, already_prepared and explicit absence of new acceptance
or remote execution. Link appropriate store/task/output IDs in PLAR and update its
status/next action against actual progress. Preparation is not completed production.
After submission continue the existing retrieval, candidate review, revision and
completion operations; failed candidates and unavailable required checks remain.

# Request and criteria handoff

Use for delegated asset work when a proposed production contract is ready to adopt, or when its consequential request/criteria change. The specialist prepares the contract; the calling agent independently compares its actual contents to the original assignment. This is an agent-to-agent review, not a new user-approval gate. Continue under established authorization when the contract is consistent.

## Specialist: return the exact proposed contract

Save a compact `request-review.json` in the consumer project. Point to existing artifacts instead of duplicating provider history or manufacturing PX2 state for a planning-only task. Its fields are:

- `version`: 1.
- `sources`: the brief and relevant consumer/reference sources, each with project-relative `path`, actual byte `sha256`, and `role`; include locators for the adopted decisions. Include the selected `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied one.
- `request`: `path`, `sha256`, `kind` (`provider_arguments` or `creative_brief`) and the actual tool name when known. Provider arguments must be the complete exact JSON to dispatch, including real reference inputs. Use a creative brief when an operation/schema has not been discovered; do not label it executable.
- `criteria`: `path` and `sha256` for the exact criteria to use. Each criterion has an ID, check, authority/basis, applicable scope and source locator. Distinguish owner/consumer requirements, specialist sample choices, observations and diagnostics.
- `choices`: the consequential specialist choices or unresolved decisions, where each appears in the request/criteria, and its reason. A criterion scoped to a chosen sample can assess that sample; it does not establish a universal project requirement.
- `resume`: existing store/task/output/job links when applicable. Omit absent production state.

Return the packet's path and SHA-256 to the caller. For PX2 production, link the saved request and Q records or an exact exported view with their state/record identity. Do not silently rebuild the request after review. Before dispatch, compare the actual arguments to the reviewed request; reference bytes/handles and non-text controls matter as much as prompt wording.

Keep a required outcome separate from the recipe proposed to achieve it. A qualitative requirement such as matching a reference or conveying a state still needs an acceptance criterion when its palette, geometry, frame count or layout are open. When demoting an unsupported recipe to a sample choice, preserve the underlying required outcome; do not leave only mechanical checks binding. Consumer code establishes its actual data/rendering behavior, not an unmeasured aesthetic quality. Attribute expert quality criteria to expert judgment where that is their basis.

Creative decisions within the assignment need not all go back to the user. For example, choosing a static first sample or a construction method is expert judgment; attributing it to an owner who specified only canvas dimensions is incorrect. Keep the choice explicit and scoped so it can be revised without changing the owner's brief. Observations alone do not become rejection rules.

Do not estimate pixel coordinates by eye and then describe them as verified. When a numerical image fact materially guides a request or verdict, retain the measurement with its source-image hash, frame and coordinate convention. When exact coordinates are unnecessary, describe the visual relationship and supply the actual reference instead.

The caller independently verifies consequential measured claims against the original image and measurement, including the coordinate convention; repeating a specialist's pixel map is not independent verification. Correct unsupported numbers before dispatch while preserving the required visual outcome.

"""Derive r2 criteria/packet from retained r1 artifacts (local helper, no network).

Changes only criterion family_sample_suitability per work/caller-review-1.json.
Original artifacts are read, never rewritten. Arguments and connection are reused.
"""
import copy
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
WORK = ROOT / "work"


def sha(path: Path) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def load(name: str):
    return json.loads((WORK / name).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def write(name: str, obj) -> Path:
    p = WORK / name
    if p.exists():
        raise SystemExit(f"refusing to overwrite {p}")
    p.write_text(json.dumps(obj, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    return p


R1_PACKET = "request-review.json"
R1_CRITERIA = "queue-ready-criteria.json"
assert sha(WORK / R1_PACKET) == "01f9fc581956766688574f5247d9b9a09273e460296f1e818fd48a2be101ea81"
assert sha(WORK / R1_CRITERIA) == "43c728d81b697ef077457f376876679a05e65018868d95c85ca8ef1396e084d0"

criteria = copy.deepcopy(load(R1_CRITERIA))
hits = [c for o in criteria["outputs"] for c in o["criteria"] if c["id"] == "family_sample_suitability"]
assert len(hits) == 1
hits[0]["check"] = (
    "Silhouette construction, edge handling and color treatment form a coherent treatment "
    "that could plausibly carry the Working/Retry/Paused members at 16x16 (including "
    "non-color-distinct motifs); the review decision is recorded."
)
# basis, scope, sources, domain, mode intentionally unchanged.

crit_path = write("queue-ready-criteria-r2.json", criteria)

packet = copy.deepcopy(load(R1_PACKET))
packet["criteria"] = {"path": "work/queue-ready-criteria-r2.json", "sha256": sha(crit_path)}
# request (arguments) and connection pointers unchanged; verify they still match bytes.

1	# Provider submission and recovery operation
2	
3	Use this operation when a PIXL production task needs an external generation request, a submitted attempt needs resumption, or a returned candidate needs to enter project state. Developing this operation is a maintainer task; only a production assignment or explicit evaluation activates PIXL.
4	
5	Read the [PX2 specification](../../../resources/spec/PIXL-2.md), its [registry](../../../runtime/pixl/registry-v2.json), and the [journal contract](../../../resources/spec/provider-recovery.md). This operation uses the explicit J.jr/op/xs extension. Existing unjournaled J and PX1 stores keep their earlier meanings; adding fields or changing a header does not manufacture durable history.
6	
7	## Required context
8	
9	- The project root, current store state/hash, task and selected planned F outputs. Use the [intake/sample operation](intake-sample.md) first if choices or criteria are missing. Sample tasks may test proposals; dependent production still needs adoption and confirmation.
10	- The actual connected provider identity, selected tool and exact inputSchema observed through this harness, with a retained discovery source, timestamp and evidence. A cached capabilities list is advisory. If live tools are absent, preserve the plan and explain the missing capability; do not invent a discovery observation.
11	- The user's established authorized scope and budget, retained as a scope string and evidence object. Existing authorization can support this record; a local tool does not grant new authority. Resolve a consequential missing budget/permission before a paid call while continuing independent work.
12	- For recovery, the saved intent and every retained observation. For import, the actual already downloaded file and evidence relating it to this returned resource. Keep credentials out of arguments, schema examples, discovery, authorization and response evidence.
13	
14	Resolve `../../../scripts/pixl.py` relative to this reference directory and invoke its absolute path using the selected Python environment. The commands below omit that common prefix. Use the same project `--root ROOT` throughout; STORE is a subdirectory of ROOT. Every mutation consumes the current `--expect HASH` and returns the next hash. Files and evidence belong in the project, outside installed resources.
15	
16	## Prepare a saved request
17	
18	Prefer the actual connected official PixelLab MCP operation when it fits the task. Use [operation and reference selection](pixellab-operations.md) first: confirm the native canvas, reference roles and output packaging. Preserve image transport identifiers with their local source hashes. The optional HTTP route below is a selected integration, not a substitute for every MCP workflow.
19	
20	When the host exposes the optional PixelLab HTTP bridge, use `pixellab_contract`
21	to inspect its retained official HTTP schema, source date and simulated/live flag.
22	It currently supports one async image operation. This is a dated HTTP contract,
23	not live MCP discovery; HTTP `image_size` is distinct from MCP width/height aliases.
24	`pixellab_prepare_image` validates and saves the request against the planned task
25	and output. Then `pixellab_submit` claims, submits once and records the response;
26	do not call local `job-dispatch` first. `pixellab_poll` observes the saved ID once
27	(allow the returned interval between real polls), and `pixellab_import_image`
28	decodes and retains a completed response as an unaccepted candidate. Each mutation
29	requires the current store hash. Continue with normal inspection and acceptance.
30	Unknown submission outcomes cannot be resubmitted; preserve and reconcile them.
31	Mocked bridge observations remain simulated, including in handoffs.
32	
33	1. Run `workflow STORE/state.px --root ROOT` and `jobs STORE/state.px --root ROOT`. Read both lifecycle blockers and existing provider attempts. An open task does not imply permission to create another remote job. Pending prepared/unknown/submitted/running work on the output must be resolved first.
34	2. Retrieve the task's focused context. Translate its intended output and relevant inputs, decisions, methods and contract into the actual tool schema. Preserve arguments exactly; describe any requirement the tool cannot express and the later acceptance check that will evaluate it.
35	3. Write a request JSON object with exactly `provider`, `tool`, `arguments`, `schema`, `discovery`, and `authorization`. `schema` is the full inputSchema object. Discovery has `source`, `observed_at`, `evidence`; authorization has `scope`, `evidence`. Evidence must be nonempty objects. Timestamps require an explicit UTC offset and at most six fractional digits. Capture observation time from the host clock when observing/recording the response (for example, Python datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()); keep provider event time separate. Do not invent a precise time from the session date, and omit optional timestamps that were not observed. Values come from the current assignment and observations, not from a bundled art fixture.
36	4. Run `job-prepare STORE JOB TASK REQUEST_JSON --outputs OUTPUT ... --expect HASH --root ROOT`. This saves exact request/schema/provenance/authorization and the relevant plan hashes. Read its cached assessment: a conflict is a reason to inspect current documentation and tool semantics, not to silently rewrite the request or substitute the cache for the observed schema. Schema validity alone cannot establish account entitlement, output quality or actual cost.
37	
38	Preparation is complete when state contains the prepared J and immutable journal X/E. No remote action has occurred. A missing tool, unresolved project requirement or missing authorization leaves useful local planning intact.
39	
40	## Claim once, then call the actual provider
41	
42	Run `job-dispatch STORE JOB --expect HASH --root ROOT`. Only a successful publication returns `dispatch_request`. It first records a local dispatch claim and moves the saved job to **unknown**, before the host sends anything. Use exactly the returned provider/tool/arguments for the one authorized host call. Do not add defaults or replace arguments after claiming; that would be a different request.
43	
44	The local command does not submit, poll, authenticate or download. `remote_executed: false` describes the local tool even when its journal later records a caller-observed success. Real provider effects remain the host's responsibility.
45	
46	Retain the response without credentials and use `job-observe STORE JOB STATE EVIDENCE_JSON --remote-id RETURNED_ID --expect HASH --root ROOT`. Accepted states submitted/running/succeeded require the actual observed identifier. A supplied failure can be recorded without inventing an ID. After identity is known, omitting `--remote-id` preserves it; it cannot be rebound. Repeat running/unknown observations only when supported by actual observations. A failed or succeeded outcome is terminal for observations.
47	
48	If submission returns no usable answer, record `unknown` with the actual timeout/transport evidence when available. Never treat the initial unknown claim as evidence that a provider received the request, and never treat a missing ID as evidence that it did not.
49	
50	For delegated work, compare the saved prepared request with the exact arguments in the [reviewed request packet](request-review.md) before dispatch. Changed arguments or criteria require an updated comparison; an unchanged reviewed contract does not require the user to repeat authorization.
51	
52	## Resume and reconcile
53	
54	Start with `jobs STORE/state.px --root ROOT`. It returns the saved request, context, event history, remote identity, candidate associations, drift and next action. Reading a request is not a new dispatch grant.
55	
56	| Saved state / issue | Next operation |
57	|---|---|
58	| Prepared, context current, no blockers | Claim with job-dispatch before one host call |
59	| Prepared, plan drift or lifecycle blocker | Resolve the specific context; abandon obsolete intent with an evidenced failed observation if appropriate, then prepare a new request ID |
60	| Unknown | Reconcile using the actual provider's documented lookup/status capabilities and retained evidence; do not dispatch or recreate |
61	| Submitted/running with ID | Inspect that exact resource using its discovered status tool, then record the observed response |
62	| Succeeded | Retrieve the actual output through the host, import local candidate bytes, then evaluate acceptance |
63	| Failed | Preserve failure, establish its consequence and any still-valid retry authorization, then use a new job ID for a new attempt |
64	| Legacy unjournaled job | Inspect its actual available history manually; do not attach a fictional journal or ignore pending work |
65	| File/hash error | Preserve the diagnostic and restore the exact retained bytes from available history/backups before continuing; do not rewrite receipts to make a changed file pass |
66	
67	A crash between claim and host submission also leaves unknown. If no provider lookup can resolve whether the request was sent, leave that uncertainty explicit and continue independent work. Elapsed time cannot authorize a retry. A confirmed non-acceptance or terminal failure may support a failed observation and a newly authorized attempt; record that evidence first. Automatic remote exactly-once delivery is not claimed.
68	
69	On `stale_write` or `store_locked`, no dispatch grant was returned. Reread the state and owner information, then reconcile the attempted local change. Do not blindly repeat job-dispatch if another writer already claimed it. Immutable blobs left by a failed publication are unreferenced preparation data; state.px is the publication authority.
70	
71	## Import and hand back to acceptance
72	
73	Download with the actual host/provider mechanism into the project. Then run `job-import STORE JOB OUTPUT CANDIDATE DOWNLOADED_PATH EVIDENCE_JSON --expect HASH --root ROOT`. DOWNLOADED_PATH is relative to ROOT. This copies a byte snapshot into the store and creates X.of for the original F, plus a retained import event and J.xs reference. It preserves the downloaded original. It does not nominate the candidate, measure the image, grant V, or finish T.
74	
75	Import rejects changed output/contract/criterion context. Keep the returned file and original history; reconcile the intended plan explicitly before associating it. A new interpretation must not relabel an old generation as though it used the new contract. Submitted observations can still be recorded while the plan has drifted.
76	
77	Retrieve the imported X to obtain its retained path/hash. Run relevant mechanical inspection, review the actual image at native and enlarged scale, and exercise the required destination checks. Follow the [intake/sample acceptance procedure](intake-sample.md) to nominate a candidate deliberately and record each Q's pass, fail or unavailable verdict. Provider success and journal-retention receipts cannot satisfy those requirements.
78	
79	The operation stops with a truthful recovery action or an imported candidate ready for its specified acceptance checks. Handoff includes the job and candidate IDs, actual observed state, retained paths, unresolved checks and the next dependency. No finished asset family or engine readiness follows from this local operation alone.

"""Author the PX2 plan-revision document for queue.ready (local helper, no network).

Reads a decoded state JSON (argv[1]), changes only criterion.ready.family_sample_suitability
(check text plus provenance to the r2 artifacts), adds S records for the r2 packet/criteria
and the caller review, bumps the revision, and writes the candidate document (argv[2]).
Commit goes through pixl_commit with the expected hash; nothing under .pixl is edited here.
"""
import hashlib
import json
import sys
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
src_path, out_path = Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2])
doc = json.loads(src_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
records = {r["id"]: r for r in doc["records"]}

NEW_CHECK = json.loads((ROOT / "work/queue-ready-criteria-r2.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
NEW_CHECK = next(c for o in NEW_CHECK["outputs"] for c in o["criteria"] if c["id"] == "family_sample_suitability")["check"]

at = datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="microseconds")


def source(rel):
    data = (ROOT / rel).read_bytes()
    lines = data.count(b"\n") or 1
    return {"ur": rel, "dg": hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest(), "ln": [1, lines], "at": at, "au": {"$symbol": "local"}}


new_sources = {
    "source.11": source("work/request-review-r2.json"),
    "source.12": source("work/queue-ready-criteria-r2.json"),
    "source.13": source("work/caller-review-1.json"),
}
for sid in new_sources:
    assert sid not in records, sid
    doc["records"].append({"id": sid, "kind": "S", "fields": new_sources[sid]})

q = records["criterion.ready.family_sample_suitability"]["fields"]
# Replace r1 packet/criteria citations (source.1, source.4) with the r2 ones; keep the rest.
q["so"] = [s for s in q["so"] if s["$ref"] not in {"source.1", "source.4"}] + [
    {"$ref": "source.11"}, {"$ref": "source.12"}, {"$ref": "source.13"}]
q["ck"] = NEW_CHECK

p = records["project"]["fields"]
p["sc"] = p["sc"] + [{"$ref": s} for s in new_sources]

doc["revision"] += 1
out_path.write_text(json.dumps(doc, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
print("revision", doc["revision"], "at", at)
